learning: If progress on the oval recovers above 0.5 while line_loss_events stays near 1, the lead was the cause and the span is kept. If progress stays low, the 16 mm footprint is probably blurring the centre signal, so test a 12 mm footprint with the same span. Compare max_error across tracks against the 0.063 to 0.065 m plateau.
notes: Restores the y = 0.05 lead with the 60 mm span and 16 mm footprints from iteration 1, with gains unchanged. This isolates whether the lead caused the iteration 1 progress collapse.
rationale: Iteration 1 changed span, footprint and lead together, and progress collapsed (oval 0.664 to 0.273, mean score 159.7 to 64.6). Line-loss events fell to 1.0 on every track and steering oscillation fell on the oval and s-bend, so the wider 60 mm span did its job on line loss. max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.065 m on every track and in both iterations, which points to transient turn-induced excursions rather than sensing dropout. The likely cause of the progress loss is the shorter lead (y 0.05 to 0.03), since the robot reacts later on bends. This iteration keeps the Builder's 60 mm span and 16 mm footprints and restores y = 0.05, so the lead is the only sensing change. Gains stay at iteration 1 values (kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45) so the lead effect is isolated from the controller. The 60 mm span is kept, so a restored lead should bring line_loss_events near 1 and oval progress back above 0.5 if the lead was the cause. Body, wheel and mass are unchanged. I expect progress to recover, but max_error is likely to stay near 0.06 m.
